text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a common practice in modern software development. When developers write new code, they regularly add it to a shared project. Each time this happens, an automated build starts on a server. This build compiles the code and runs tests to check that everything works correctly. The main goal is to catch issues early, before they become big problems. CI pipelines make this process smooth by automating each step, from building to testing. As a result, teams can find and fix bugs quickly, keep the software stable, and deliver updates to users faster and with more confidence.
